film.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
film.promptPreamble: Photorealistic cinematic short about a lighthouse keeper lighting the lamp at nightfall on a windswept coast. Consistent look across every shot: cold blue twilight exteriors warming to amber lamp light interiors, real weather, sea mist, shallow depth of field, film grain. The keeper is a weathered man in his sixties, grey stubble, navy wool coat. Realtime speed, brisk natural motion. Audio is wind, sea, and machine room tone only. Keep every frame subtitle-free and free of any watermark or on-screen lettering.

cards.text: Every night, the light goes on.

shots.prompt:
The opening frame matches the provided keyframe: the lighthouse on its cliff at last light.
Shot 1: aerial wide pushing in over the headland; wind flattens the long grass in fast waves and gulls scatter off the cliff edge; the tower stands right of frame above a grey breaking sea; <wind gusting, surf hitting rock far below>.
Shot 2: cut to a low ground-level medium tracking right; the keeper strides across the wet grass toward the tower door, coat snapping behind him; he crosses frame left to right; <boots on wet stone, coat fabric cracking in the gust>.
Shot 3: hard cut to a tight shot on the door; he hauls the iron door open and steps through, then swings it shut behind him; the doorway fills frame; <hinge groan, a heavy slam, the wind dropping to a muffled roar>.

The opening frame matches the provided keyframe: the keeper mid-climb on the spiral staircase, lantern raised.
Shot 1: medium tracking beside him on the curve, rising with the climb; he takes the iron steps two at a time and the swinging lantern throws amber light racing across the curved white wall; he stays screen centre behind the stair rail; <boots ringing on iron treads, the lantern handle rattling>.
Shot 2: cut to a low angle straight up the stairwell; the spiral corkscrews away above him as his lantern light climbs the wall ahead of it; he is small at the bottom of frame; <wind moaning down the stone shaft>.
Shot 3: cut to a close profile pushing in; he clears the top step, sets his jaw and looks up at the lamp room hatch; his face fills the right of frame, lit from below; <a last footfall, a hard breath, the hatch latch clicking>.

The opening frame matches the provided keyframe: the keeper at the Fresnel lens, hand on the ignition valve, lamp dark.
Shot 1: locked-off medium, the camera completely static on a tripod for the whole beat; he cranks the brass valve open and strikes the igniter twice; his hands work at frame centre against the glass; <a gas hiss building, two sharp flint strikes>.
Shot 2: cut to a macro on the burner, camera still locked; the mantle catches and flares white, light exploding out through the cut glass; the flame fills frame; <an ignition thump, a rising electrical hum>.
Shot 3: cut to a static wide of the lamp room; the lens starts to rotate and throws hard bars of light across his face and the walls, sea mist crossing the beam; he stands left of frame, the lens right; <the deep mechanical turn of the gearing, wind against the gallery glass>.

The opening frame matches the provided keyframe: the lit tower at night, the first beam breaking out over black water.
Shot 1: extreme wide from out at sea, craning up; the beam swings across the heaving water and rakes the cliff face; the tower is small and burning at frame centre; <surf detonating on rock, the muffled turn of the lamp>.
Shot 2: cut to a mid shot at the gallery rail, arcing around the tower; the beam sweeps straight past the lens and flares the frame white, then clears; the wet rail cuts across the lower third; <a hard wind buffet, the mechanical rhythm of the lamp>.
Shot 3: hard cut to a top-down aerial climbing away; the beam scythes a full circle over open sea, whitecaps racing beneath it; the lighthouse sits dead centre and shrinks; <open wind, distant surf>.

The opening frame matches the provided keyframe: a small fishing boat far out in heavy swell, the beam reaching it.
Shot 1: wide at sea level riding the swell; the boat pitches hard over a crest and the beam catches its wheelhouse; the boat is left of frame, the far light right; <hull slamming into water, a diesel engine labouring>.
Shot 2: cut to a close shot through the streaming wheelhouse glass; the skipper spins the wheel hand over hand and the bow swings toward the light; his hands and the wet glass fill frame; <the wheel chain running, rain driving on glass>.
Shot 3: cut to a wide stern view trailing the boat; it settles onto the new heading and runs straight at the distant beam, its wake straightening behind it; the light sits on the horizon at frame centre; <the engine steadying, surf, wind easing>.
